name: GitLab Senior Customer Success Operations Manager Operating System + Cover Letter

tracks.label: Book of Business
tracks.objective: Prioritize customer segments and accounts around health, renewal timing, coverage, risk, and next action.

tracks.label: CS Operating Cadence

tracks.label: Health & Renewal Reporting

tracks.label: Process Improvement
tracks.objective: Turn ambiguous CS friction into scoped workstreams, owners, acceptance criteria, rollout, and adoption.

tracks.label: Capacity & Segmentation

tracks.label: Operational Risk

public_sources.label: GitLab Senior Customer Success Operations Manager

candidate_evidence: Check Point Customer Success Operations: increased dedicated CSM coverage for >$50K accounts to 99% and maintained onboarding outreach within a two-week SLA.
Managed 20–40 SaaS accounts totaling approximately $3M ARR; portfolio visibility improved from about 40% to 99%, churn reduced to under 30%, and team efficiency improved 30%.
Dedrone: standardized enterprise onboarding to about one month, increased engagement 25%, increased renewals 20%, and supported stakeholder buy-in for an approximately $3M AWS-hosted solution.
Built and operated Salesforce, Custify, Jira, and Salesforce-to-Jira workflow/reporting patterns; led QBR/EBR, health/risk, escalation, onboarding, and adoption motions.
Led distributed customer-facing support teams; Cofense enablement and automation contributed to 30% ticket deflection, 40% fewer support tickets, and a 30-minute faster first response.
Current proof-of-work includes AI-assisted workflow automation and browser-local Customer Success operating systems built through Clintware.
disclosure: Candidate-built Clintware operating prototype using public GitLab role context with clearly synthetic sample data. It is not an official GitLab product, customer tenant, private process description, or representation of real GitLab customers.
persistence_reason: Candidate/demo workspace state is single-browser and does not require shared server-authoritative storage.

why_company.draft:
GitLab stands out because the role is explicitly about the kind of operating work I have repeatedly gravitated toward: turning ambiguity into a system that Customer Success can actually use.  The combination of customer-health reporting, renewal cadence, book-of-business management, planning, documentation, and cross-functional Revenue Operations is closely aligned to how I have worked across Customer Success and Support.

At Check Point, I helped move portfolio visibility from roughly 40% to 99%, built reporting and workflow structure across Salesforce, Custify, and Jira, and supported a model that reached 99% dedicated CSM coverage for accounts above $50K.  I have also managed enterprise portfolios directly, so I understand how an operating decision lands on the CSM and the customer rather than treating the process as an abstract systems exercise.

GitLab's all-remote, documentation-heavy culture and expectation that AI be used as a productivity multiplier are also a strong fit for how I work now.  I use AI to accelerate analysis and repeatable work, while keeping human validation over metrics, customer commitments, and consequential decisions.

I would bring a practical operator's perspective: Make the source of truth clearer, remove avoidable manual work, and make the next decision easier to see.

cover_letter.draft:
Dear GitLab Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Customer Success Operations Manager role because it closely matches the work I have done at the intersection of Customer Success, systems, reporting, and process improvement.

At Check Point, I helped improve portfolio visibility from roughly 40% to 99%, supported 99% dedicated CSM coverage for accounts above $50K, and built operating workflows across Salesforce, Custify, and Jira.  I also managed 20 to 40 SaaS accounts totaling approximately $3M ARR, which gave me the field perspective to understand what Customer Success teams actually need from their operating systems, reporting, renewal cadence, and cross-functional partners.

My strongest work tends to begin with an ambiguous operating problem.  I define the decision that needs to be made, identify the data and ownership required, build the process or reporting path, and then stay with it through rollout and adoption.  That approach has also informed the AI-assisted workflow systems I now build through Clintware, where automation handles repeatable preparation while human judgment remains responsible for validation and consequential decisions.

GitLab's emphasis on documentation, iteration, systems thinking, and practical use of AI makes this role particularly compelling.  I would be interested in helping the Customer Success organization make health, renewal, capacity, and book-of-business decisions more consistent and easier to act on.

Thank you for your consideration.

Clinton Kosh

values.name: Speed with Quality
